newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia urges Taleban to negotiate to end Afghan war.
newsitem.headline: Russia urges Taleban to negotiate to end Afghan war.

text.p: Russia called on the Islamic Taleban militia in Afghanistan on Monday to negotiate a political compromise to end the country's civil war.

Deputy Foreign Minister Viktor Posuvalyuk told Interfax news agency following a trip to Pakistan that he had met a Taleban representative who assured him of the movement's desire for normal relations with Russia.

Moscow, which has troops along the Afghan frontier in Tajikistan, has been alarmed by the success of the Taleban, fearing their purist brand of Islam could stir tensions and push refugees into the already fragile former Soviet states along Russia's Central Asian flank.

Posuvalyuk said he used his contact with the Taleban "to once again thoroughly and precisely draw attention to the need to seek political and not military means to end the crisis and achieve lasting peace and accord in Afghanistan".
While pressing for the creation of a broad coalition government acceptable to all parties in the country, the Russian diplomat insisted Moscow had no wish to interfere in Afghan affairs.
"One should not identify Russia's current policy with that period when Soviet forces were in Afghanistan," he said, recalling Moscow's bloody 10-year intervention from 1979-89.
Posuvalyuk said he welcomed assurances from his Pakistani counterparts that Islamabad was ready to work with Russia to promote a peaceful solution in Afghanistan.

Some analysts say Pakistan has backed the Taleban, although Pakistan denies this. Former Soviet states had supported an alliance of anti-Taleban forces in northern Afghanistan which split last month, allowing the Taleban to gain territory.
